reason: The supplied assembly shows a concrete cost in the full512 packing block: it loads 32 vectors, moves them into ZA, then writes the packed panel to scratch, repeating this work across 64 row blocks. This makes coordinated traversal and B-layout experiments relevant to the timed path, but instruction counts alone do not establish a performance bottleneck or predict a gain. I rank ZA reuse first because it changes traversal while retaining the existing helper-free kernel; loop_order is related and carries substantial pointer and coverage risk. B packing and prefetch are distinct but add timed work without supplied cache evidence. Transpose fusion and a_transpose are lower because they replace substantial paths, and a_transpose affects only the general fallback, not the n=512 target. Tail alignment addresses unconfirmed correctness assumptions. cache_blocking needs an unavailable panel64 helper. The two K-loop proposals rely on a two-step body not present in the supplied current assembly; address_generation's 256-iteration proposal would also skip K values in that one-step body. All proposed benefits remain unverified.
